topics.title: Matilda's discontent and the invitation to the ball

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Matilda is always unhappy with her modest life and how her husband differs from her.
Describe Matilda's reaction to the Minister's invitation and how the problem of the dress is solved.

topics.title: Borrowing the necklace and the night of the ball

concepts.learning_objective: Recount how Matilda solves the problem of having no jewel by borrowing from Mme Forestier.
Interpret Matilda's success at the ball and her hurried departure as signs of her character.

topics.title: The loss of the necklace and its replacement

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the steps the Loisels take to find the lost necklace and to buy time.
Explain how the Loisels raise money to replace the necklace and evaluate their decision to hide the loss.

topics.title: Ten years of poverty and hard work

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the hardships the Loisels accept in order to repay their debt.
Analyse how ten years of labour change Matilda's appearance and character.

topics.title: The final revelation, setting and message
topics.ncert_sections: Ending, Think about it, Talk about it

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the irony of Mme Forestier's revelation that the necklace was false.
Identify the author and the clues that show the story is set in France among French speakers.
Evaluate the story's message about pride, honesty and contentment.
